column8: Tue 17 Nov: store, RESIDENCY and LAURA; corrects Q18-036's 'never published the founders' sum': CSM 2004 gives more than $6 million from Eric Carle, while the $18m was sought in sponsorships; the building/endowment split is still unpublished; in Taiwan the founder pays first (Q11e), never 'the largest share'.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3.0 clause beside the Taiwan's-founders reserve, but fix the contrast: Laura's reserve pays her $50,000 a year, a base and not the residency's whole budget (H9-119), so never set her ten against Carle's whole spending as years covered; the right contrast is dated and spendable against perpetual and market-priced (Q9b-030); $444,545 and 111.4% are NUMBERS 8h but are re-sized Wed 18 Nov; spending is ProPublica's IRS data and Schedule D was read in excerpt, so S 3.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q9b-001 (Yaddo's board-designated share with the board's own power to lift it, the stronger row); Carle's 81.63% quasi-endowment adds only a creator's name; store only.

Tue 17 Nov: store, the Carle instance of Q101-011 (endowments arrive long after opening) and Q18-036's challenge grant; fix the use: the money came as gifts (a $2m gift, half of it matched), not pledges; a pledge is owed and Laura's floor owned, so never blur the two words.

Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 6 (gifts about three-quarters of revenue, twenty years on), which is read at source in the museum's own report; this row rests on ProPublica's IRS data, and its 8-of-12 deficit years are weakened by its own disanalogy (depreciation, timing of multi-year gifts).

Tue 17 Nov: store, RESIDENCY, the current Carle figure: 24 years on, gifts 76% of operating revenue and the endowment draw 7.4% of spending (preliminary; the report says the budget balanced); use only as no year of Laura's ten waits on an ask, never as if her residency asks no one (the case lets co-sponsors fund support beyond her commitment).

Tue 17 Nov: store only; a founder's yearly giving fell about 97% in four years (ProPublica's IRS data; recipients not itemised, so not all of it went to the museum); the IPS l.9 career point is already carried by stronger rows.

Tue 17 Nov: store only, UNVERIFIED (grant years rest on aggregator sites, filings not opened, fiscal years differ); if ever used, say only that the founders' second foundation still gives the museum millions a year from an estate that arrived long after opening, beside Q101-011.

Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 or 3a, the card's top row (quotes spot-checked at source tonight): the closest precedent planned its running money on the very sources the case says teams may not rely on; fix the use: at today's rates most of each payment is owned from January 2027 and all ten from January 2028 (NUMBERS 1, the $2,388 top-up), never owned from Jan 2027; the heirs, not Schulz, built it.

Tue 17 Nov: pairs with row 9 (quotes spot-checked at source): a director's minimum of 200,000 visitors met 35% then 28% (Keel arithmetic); fix the use to TNA l.15's words, each payment rests on a dedicated instrument, not merely a forecast, rather than rest on no forecast; a ticket forecast, not an investment one.

Tue 17 Nov: store, RESIDENCY: what became of row 9's museum, 22 years on: investment income about a fifth of spending, yet deficits in three of five years (ProPublica's IRS data, so S 3; most assets are building and collection; pandemic years included).

Tue 17 Nov: 3b or 3e store: a cartoonist's endowment did not protect a museum that rented its site (NPQ, read at source), so operating money and the building are separate questions (IPS l.15); it reopened in 2017, so never say it closed for good.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; one of the 16 cases behind claim 1's verdict (an illustrator gave the art and a place, not running money).

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 store beside Q50: in 2009 an illustrator's museum held $3m against a $4.7m budget and expected to borrow from it, in the recession in which IPS l.9 says a writer's income comes later and smaller; say can, never fall together (Q50); Berkshire Eagle read in excerpt.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or LAURA clause: the one case where the source of running money (her works and part of the copyright) was handed over before opening, a picture-book artist's licences, the same kind of income the case says funds Laura's 2028 deposit; a royalty stream is not a sum owned or dated, and that is the contrast.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; drop 'the same order as Laura's plan': the museum says the building was financed through donations and royalties, so the split is not clean, and the card's own claim 3 forbids a lineage.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a clause (card's best four): the best-run creator foundation found keeps running money and building money in separate named pots, as IPS l.15 and l.17 do, but filled them over 47 years and invests them without dates; say it took decades, never that Chihiro matched dates.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q9b-001 (a board's label can be lifted); by its own disanalogy, relabelling to match a change in the law is not spending, so it adds little; activity report read in excerpt.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 10 (ticket forecasts miss), with a milder miss (70-81% of target) nearly fifty years on; reports read in excerpt.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q101-011 (running money arrives at the founder's death); the asset series is from Instrumentl's IRS data with filings not opened, so S 2.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e honest-limit store: money behind a residency does not by itself keep it running (site and people too); fix the figure: $40-57m rests on IRS-data sites, so say tens of millions or ProPublica's $42,084,100 with its year; the 2018-2022 gap is partly the pandemic and the reasons for 2018-19 were not found.

Tue 17 Nov: 3b store: a founder's written wish for a museum failed on site and access, not money; supports the case's flexibility as the project develops; US zoning, and Taiwan's land rules are untested and out of scope.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a store, the illustrator instance of Q101-002 (foundations without money at the start sell assets to run), which IPS l.11 rules out for the ten; art is not shares and the sale was a choice; NYT read in excerpt, spending from ProPublica.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a picture-book maker's foundation ran on his yearly income while he lived and on his royalties after; grants, not a place.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 24; the 990's other income is not labelled royalties (an inference on ProPublica's IRS data) and the later year is undated, so S 2.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a city-run museum, not creator-founded, and FY2020 is the pandemic; never read it as a fall in Laura's genre (the 2023 fall was manga's, card Q108).

Tue 17 Nov: store only; the 46% rests on a cost column whose label is partly garbled; a city filling a museum's gap each year is the co-sponsor money the case allows beyond Laura's commitment, already in the store.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; fix the use: her flexibility's uses are IPS l.15's three (overruns, a stronger Taiwan dollar, a co-sponsor falling short), and a repair lump thirty years on is none of them and lies past 2042.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; fix the use: Takarazuka's squeeze is a ten-year structural shortfall, not a downturn, so it cannot show budgets falling in the same downturn (Q50); at most, a public sponsor's budget can tighten and pass costs to users; a Japanese city, never Taiwan's government (CANON B4).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the NT$1 licence quote is read at source, but the lease and funding history rest on zh.wikipedia, so S 2; not creator-founded.

Tue 17 Nov: store only, zh.wikipedia only (UNVERIFIED); fix the use: owned running money does not avoid a lost lease or a missing use licence, which are site risks; close kin of Q100-030 (IT Park, a lease ended).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a Taiwanese cartoonist's own small place paid in one lump; no running-cost figures, so it does no investing job.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; an absence, not proof; Taiwan's state, not the creator, staged the legacy show.

Tue 17 Nov: LAURA store; Taiwan's best-known picture-book artist built a licensing company and no place of his was found; say no residency of his was found, never that a residency is the rarer path (two absences give no rate).

Tue 17 Nov: 3d beside H7-070 (quotes spot-checked at source tonight): Marvel paid $100,000 of a $1 million pledge and went bankrupt; a cartoonist's museum, so closer to Laura than Lehman; a pledge is owed, Laura's floor owned; a son's recollection, not accounts, and the museum closed five years later with rent also in play (row 36), so say only the first $100,000 came and never that the pledge alone closed it.

Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 12 (rent, not the founder's death, moved or ended a cartoon museum); the $650,000 rent quote is read at source (spot-checked), the first move and the grant's size are Wikipedia only.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; an illustrator's national centre bought its building first and raised the running money after; far bigger than Laura's residency.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a store beside the nobody-can-run reserve: an illustrator's centre borrowed its working capital (a GBP 1m social investment) while it paid for its building; Laura borrows nothing; the AHF page is undated.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; an Australian case, used only if it earns its place (not here): her royalties went to charities and the house had to be rescued by a council.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a residency for children's book makers carries a creator's name and none of her money.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a creator's island cottage given without running money is now rented as a residency; no figures.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e store, the honest counter-case: a graphic novelist's school lasted twenty years on tuition and a $250,000 start-up credit line, renting before it owned; the case bars program fees only for the ten payments, so this is another model, not a failure.
